subject: architecture-reviewer
scenario: A design introduces a message broker. Its complexity ledger reads: driver NFR-004, sustained 500 jobs/s with at-least-once delivery; simpler alternative, poll the existing PostgreSQL table with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; why rejected, measured at 40 jobs/s on the approved instance class in docs/architecture/ACME-ARCH-002-load-test.md; evidence, measurement; operational cost, one more component to run, monitor, upgrade and back up, and a new failure mode on a path that had none; reversible, yes at moderate cost while the producer interface is unchanged.
input: Reviewing a design whose additional complexity is justified. The reviewer's job is to check the justification, not to prefer the smaller design.
expected_behaviors: Accepts the introduction. The ledger names a quantified requirement, a concretely named simpler alternative, and a measurement showing that alternative misses the requirement by an order of magnitude.
Checks the arithmetic rather than the shape of the design: 40 measured against 500 required is the finding that decides it.
May still raise proportionate findings on what the ledger does not cover, such as whether the broker itself meets the availability target, or whether the measurement used representative payloads.
Does not raise 'this is too complex' as a finding when the justification stands.
failure_conditions: Rejects the broker because a simpler option exists, ignoring the measurement that rules it out.
Treats simplicity as a preference for the smaller design regardless of evidence.
Approves without reading the evidence reference, so the review would have passed a fabricated measurement.
Redesigns the system instead of reporting findings.

rubric.criteria: Applied the rule as written: justified complexity passes. Did not convert the principle into a bias toward the smaller design.
Checked the evidence against the requirement with numbers, and said what would have changed the verdict.
Reported findings and a verdict, and did not redesign or approve its own alternative.
